comparator.sourceNotes: The formal 2026–2027 regulations list 180 EC for September 2026 entrants, with a 30 EC minor and three of five 10 EC portfolio seminars. The published seminar prerequisites still use older course names. The credit structure is supported, while entry to two of the illustrated seminars remains to be confirmed for this cohort.

core: Language processing, cognition, brain and development
Language use, rhetoric, meaning, persuasion and communication across textual and media forms
Text data, large-language-model methods and human-centred reflection on language technologies
Experimental statistics, evidence synthesis and critical analysis of language, mind and communication

trace: Uses ethical and psychological frameworks to examine privacy, fairness and responsibility in AI.
Uses formal logic, sets and relations to build analytical foundations for studying structure and meaning.
Cleans, joins, analyses and visualises data, including text, in R.
Evaluates classification and prediction methods on held-out datasets, supporting later text modelling.
Implements and evaluates neural networks, with work on text prediction and transformers.
Writes and tests Python programs with functions and data structures for later computational text work.
Builds mathematical modelling and optimisation foundations for later machine-learning work.
Designs qualitative research using interviews, observations and systematic interpretation of qualitative evidence.
Examines nervous systems, brain anatomy and comparative methods for studying behaviour.
Studies sensory processing and goal-directed behaviour using cognitive neuroscience and neuropsychology.
Uses cognitive experiments and research design to study attention, memory and higher functions involved in language processing.
Directly studies speech comprehension, production, acquisition, bilingualism, aphasia and dyslexia and uses experimental approaches to language processing.
Introduces the brain, behaviour, learning and behavioural and imaging methods used in cognitive science.
Examines social cognition and influence, including how the presence and behaviour of others affect communication.
Uses experimental design, multivariable models and R to analyse behavioural evidence.
Studies clinical communication, interviewing and the psychological and social effects of health conditions.
Uses systematic review and meta-analysis to compare evidence and effect sizes across behavioural studies.
Examines cognitive and social development across the lifespan using theories, cases and an interview.
Analyses how arguments, delivery and rhetorical choices affect audiences.
Uses grammar, modality, deixis and discourse to explain how linguistic choices shape meaning in texts.
Applies and adapts oral storytelling, public speaking and debate activities for school pupils.
Uses framing, verbal and nonverbal communication, and argumentation to evaluate persuasive messages.
Uses close reading, genre and form to investigate how textual choices create meaning.

alternatives.label: Language processing, cognition & communication
alternatives.concept: Study how people understand and produce language. Combine psycholinguistics with cognition, developmental psychology, text analysis and research methods, and explore how computers process text.
alternatives.labelReason: Psycholinguistics anchors the programme, with substantial cognitive science, behavioural methods, linguistic analysis of texts and selected language technology.
progression: Brain & Behavior precedes Psycholinguistics and later cognitive and developmental courses. Statistics precedes evidence synthesis. Programming, Mathematical Methods and introductory data science precede neural networks and text modelling.

candidates.label: Clinical linguistics, neurolinguistics and speech-language disorders

selection.assessment: One provisional option responds to language processing and language use through psycholinguistics, cognitive science and research methods. Formal logic and stylistics cannot support a separate structural linguistics option without sustained syntax, phonology and morphology. General psychology and neuroscience do not provide clinical language assessment, treatment or specialist language neuroimaging.

blocks: Both address language processing and experimental psycholinguistics. Groningen devotes a separate course to a psycholinguistics project.
Both examine applications of AI alongside ethics and effects on people and society. Groningen also studies language, multimodality and AI literacy.
Both support empirical research using statistical analysis. UCR applies multivariable models and experimental methods to behavioural research.
Structural, clinical and specialist linguistics gaps

notes.text: UCR brings together psycholinguistics, cognition, behavioural research and text analysis. Groningen also has a sequence in phonology, syntax, semantics and language change, as well as clinical assessment, neuroimaging and specialist graduation seminars.

audience.programmeDescription: Linguistics at the University of Groningen studies how people learn and use language, how languages are structured, and what happens when language is affected by a disorder.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related study in psycholinguistics and cognitive science. Groningen provides a dedicated sequence in language structure, clinical linguistics and research on language and the brain.
